newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - July 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Chittagong Feeder Trade Committee, a Singapore based organisation of ship owners, has decided to impose congestion surcharge on container cargo at the Chittagong Port from August 15.
Some 187 Burmese Rohingya refugees were repatriated to Burma on Sunday, resuming the process after 80 days.
The Indian State Minister for Water Resources, Sis Ram Ola, on Sunday said India would do everything for the implementation of the Ganges water sharing treaty.
Bangladesh will soon import 100,000 tonnes for Diamonium Phosphate (DAP) fertiliser.
A top level meeting on law and order on Sunday warned stern action against unruly activities by some "fundamentalist" groups.
Dutch Minister for Development Cooperation, Jan P Pronk, arrived in Dhaka on Sunday on a eight-day visit to Bangladesh.
Russian ambassador in Dhaka on Sunday said Moscow was keen to raise its assistance and cooperation in exploration of oil, gas and other mineral resources and in power generation in Bangladesh.
Burmese Rohingya refugees clashed with officials at two camps over a repatriation dispute on Sunday, injuring 15 people.
